Google Cloud

Cloud


Products


Compute

Introduction

Google Cloud's compute services provide the foundational building blocks to run applications in virtual machines, containers, or serverless environments. As a Cloud DevOps Engineer or Cloud Architect, understanding these services is crucial for designing scalable, resilient, and cost-effective infrastructure. Compute services range from low-level VM instances to high-level managed platforms and serverless computing, offering flexibility based on use cases.

These services are designed to:

  • Run web apps, APIs, batch jobs, and backend processing.
  • Support hybrid and multi-cloud architectures.
  • Offer automation, autoscaling, and integration with other GCP services.
  • Enable containerized and serverless deployments.

Compute Engine

IaaS offering that allows you to create and run virtual machines (VMs) on demand.

Use cases:

  • Lift-and-shift legacy applications
  • Custom compute workloads
  • High-performance computing (HPC)
  • Running containerized applications with full control

Key features:

  • Fully customizable VM configurations
  • Support for custom images, GPUs, and local SSDs
  • Preemptible VMs for cost optimization
  • Instance groups and autoscaling
  • Managed instance templates
  • Integration with startup scripts and metadata server
  • Use Instance Templates + Managed Instance Groups for scalability.
  • Apply OS policies and patching using OS Config.
  • Leverage VPC and IAM for network and access control.
  • Monitor performance with Ops Agent and Cloud Monitoring.

Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)

A managed Kubernetes service to deploy, manage, and scale containerized applications using Kubernetes.

Use cases:

  • Microservices architecture
  • Continuous deployment pipelines
  • Hybrid and multi-cloud container strategies
  • Multi-tenant workloads with namespaces

Key features:

  • Autopilot mode for hands-off node management
  • Native Kubernetes integration
  • Support for Istio, Anthos, and Cloud Run for Anthos
  • Auto-upgrades, auto-repair, and horizontal pod autoscaling
  • Node pools, taints, and affinity rules
  • Use Workload Identity to secure access to GCP services.
  • Apply Pod Security Policies and enable network policies.
  • Integrate with Cloud Logging and Monitoring.
  • Use Binary Authorization for secure deployments.

Cloud Functions

A lightweight serverless compute solution to run single-purpose functions in response to events.

Use cases:

  • Event-driven microservices
  • Automation scripts
  • Webhooks or HTTP APIs
  • Data processing on file upload or pub/sub triggers

Key features:

  • Triggers: HTTP, Cloud Storage, Pub/Sub, Firestore
  • Auto-scaling from 0 to thousands of instances
  • Integrated IAM and Secrets Manager
  • Pay-per-use pricing (based on invocations)
  • Ideal for small, decoupled tasks.
  • Use environment variables and Secrets Manager securely.
  • Cold starts may affect latency—tune accordingly.
  • Consider using Functions Framework locally for testing.

Cloud Run

A serverless container platform for running stateless containers over HTTP.

Use cases:

  • Deploy containerized microservices without managing infrastructure
  • Hosting APIs and backend services
  • CI/CD pipelines

Key features:

  • Supports any containerized app (built with any language/runtime)
  • Scales to zero when idle
  • Easy GitHub/GitLab integration
  • Secure by default with HTTPS and IAM
  • Great balance of container flexibility and serverless simplicity.
  • Stateless: avoid using persistent storage within the service.
  • Use traffic splitting for gradual rollouts.
  • Can be integrated with GKE, Pub/Sub, or Eventarc.

App Engine (Standard & Flexible)

A fully managed Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) for building scalable web apps and APIs.

Use cases:

  • Hosting web frontends or REST APIs
  • Rapid development of scalable apps
  • Multi-version deployments and A/B testing

Key features:

  • Standard environment: auto-scaling, supports specific runtimes (e.g., Python, Node.js)
  • Flexible environment: customizable runtimes, uses Compute Engine under the hood
  • Integrated services: Memcache, Task Queues, Cron jobs
  • Standard is cheaper and faster to scale; flexible is more customizable.
  • Supports traffic splitting and versioning.
  • Great for teams who want to abstract server management.
  • Logs and monitoring are fully integrated.

Batch

A fully managed batch processing service for running batch jobs on Compute Engine or container environments.

Use cases:

  • Data transformation, rendering, and ETL jobs
  • Genomics and financial simulations
  • Parallel computing workloads

Key features:

  • Cost-optimized VM provisioning (includes preemptible VMs)
  • Flexible scheduling and resource-based scaling
  • Container and script-based task support
  • Supports job dependencies and job queuing.
  • Ideal for non-interactive, large-scale workloads.
  • Consider integrating with Cloud Storage and BigQuery for I/O.

Storage

Introduction

Storage and database services in Google Cloud are designed to reliably store and manage data at scale, across structured, semi-structured, and unstructured formats. These services support everything from object storage for backups and logs, to high-performance transactional databases, to scalable NoSQL solutions for real-time applications.

As a Cloud DevOps Engineer or Cloud Architect, understanding when to use each storage/database option is critical for performance, cost optimization, scalability, and operational simplicity.

Object & file storage

Cloud Storage (GCS)

Object storage

Use cases: Store unstructured data like media files, logs, backups, ML datasets.

Key features:

  • Multi-regional, regional, nearline (30d) and coldline/archive (90–365d) tiers.
  • Lifecycle management, versioning, encryption (including CMEK).
  • Integration with CDN, Dataflow, BigQuery, and more.
  • Use signed URLs or IAM for secure access.
  • Enables serverless backups, static website hosting, and data lake solutions.

Filestore

Managed network file system (NFS)

Use cases: High-performance file system for GKE, Compute Engine apps, CMS systems.

Key features:

  • Fully managed NFSv3 with standard and high-scale performance tiers.
  • Ideal for shared stateful applications.
  • Excellent for lift-and-shift apps needing POSIX compliance.
  • Integrates with Anthos and Kubernetes volumes.

Persistent Disks (PD)

Block storage for Compute Engine & GKE

Use cases: VM boot disks, databases, applications requiring fast IOPS.

Key features:

  • SSD and balanced HDD/standard tiers.
  • Snapshots, encryption, regional replication.
  • Good for stateful apps in GKE with StatefulSets.
  • Attach/detach volumes dynamically in CI/CD pipelines.

Relational Databases (SQL)

Cloud SQL

Managed relational database service

Supports: MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server

Use cases: Web applications, business systems, analytics.

Key features:

  • Automated backups, HA with failover, IAM-based auth.
  • Maintenance, patching, scaling, and replication built-in.
  • Easy migration from on-premises.
  • Use private IPs and VPC peering to secure traffic.

Cloud Spanner

Type: Globally distributed, horizontally scalable relational DB

Use cases: Global apps, financial systems, gaming backends.

Key features:

  • ANSI SQL + relational consistency with NoSQL scalability.
  • Strong consistency, global transactions.
  • Perfect for multi-region architectures.
  • Expensive but eliminates need for complex sharding logic.

AlloyDB

Type: High-performance, PostgreSQL-compatible managed DB

Use cases: Analytics + transactional workloads, PostgreSQL modernization.

Key features:

  • Up to 4x faster than standard PostgreSQL.
  • Supports vector queries (AI/ML-ready).
  • Best for advanced OLAP/OLTP hybrid applications.
  • Integrates well with Vertex AI and BigQuery.

NoSQL Databases

Cloud Firestore

Type: Serverless NoSQL document DB

Use cases: Mobile/web apps, real-time collaboration tools.

Key features:

  • Realtime updates, offline support, horizontal scalability.
  • ACID transactions, strong consistency.
  • Integrates natively with Firebase.
  • IAM integration for granular control, useful in serverless APIs.

Cloud Bigtable

Type: Wide-column NoSQL DB

Use cases: Time-series data, IoT, telemetry, recommendation engines.

Key features:

  • Massive throughput (10+ TB tables, millions of ops/sec).
  • HBase API compatible.
  • Choose when you need petabyte-scale and low-latency reads/writes.
  • Use with Dataflow, Pub/Sub, and BigQuery pipelines.

Memorystore

Type: Managed in-memory store (Redis / Memcached)

Use cases: Caching, session stores, gaming leaderboards.

Key features:

  • Fully managed with high availability and failover.
  • Secure with VPC support and IAM integration.
  • Reduces database latency significantly.
  • Redis is common for token/session management in web stacks.

Data Warehousing & Analytics

BigQuery

Type: Serverless data warehouse

Use cases: Real-time analytics, dashboards, BI, ML on structured data.

Key features:

  • SQL-based, scalable to petabytes.
  • Native ML (BigQuery ML), BI Engine, federated queries.
  • Serverless = no infrastructure to manage.
  • Use scheduled queries and data exports to automate reporting.

Other

Transfer Service

Use cases: Move data from AWS S3, Azure, or on-prem.

Key features:

  • Supports online/offline migration.
  • Fast parallel transfer and resumable sessions.
  • Good for batch jobs or cutover strategies.

Backup and DR

Use cases: Centralized backup and disaster recovery for Compute Engine, GKE, SQL.

Key features:

  • Automated policies, cross-region backup, point-in-time recovery.
  • Important for compliance and cost-effective RTO/RPO management.

Identity & security

Introduction

Security in the cloud is shared responsibility—while Google secures the infrastructure, it's your job to define and enforce access controls, identity management, and data protection.

The Identity & Security product suite in GCP provides the foundational tools to:

  • Manage who can access what and how.
  • Protect sensitive data.
  • Detect, investigate, and respond to threats.
  • Ensure compliance and governance.

A strong understanding of these services is mission-critical for architecting secure-by-design cloud systems.

Identity & Access Management (IAM)

Identity and Access Management (IAM)

Fine-grained, role-based access control (RBAC) to GCP resources.

Use cases: Define "who" (user, group, service account) can perform "what" action on "which" resource.

Key concepts:

  • Principals: Users, service accounts, Google groups.
  • Roles: Basic (Owner, Editor, Viewer), Predefined (e.g., Storage Admin), Custom.
  • IAM Policies: Bind principals to roles at project, folder, or org level.
  • Use least privilege principle and custom roles.
  • Avoid using primitive roles (Owner/Editor).
  • Regularly audit IAM policies using Policy Analyzer or IAM Recommender.

Cloud Identity

Identity as a Service (IDaaS) for managing users, devices, and apps.

Use cases: Central identity management for cloud and SaaS apps.

Features:

  • Directory management, SSO, MFA enforcement, endpoint security.
  • Integrate with Google Workspace or third-party IdPs.
  • Helps enforce context-aware access policies.

Workforce Identity Federation

Allows external identities (e.g., Azure AD, Okta, GitHub) to access GCP without service account keys.

Use cases: Multi-cloud environments, federated CI/CD pipelines.

Features:

  • Avoids long-lived service account keys.
  • Great for ephemeral access in CI/CD and cross-cloud automation.

Workload Identity Federation

Maps Kubernetes or external workloads to Google IAM identities.

Use cases: Secure, short-lived credentials for GKE or non-Google workloads accessing GCP APIs.

Features:

  • Essential for Zero Trust and least-privilege workloads.
  • Use in place of storing keys in Kubernetes secrets.

Security & Threat Detection

Security Command Center (SCC)

Centralized security and risk management dashboard for GCP.

Use cases: View vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, threats, and compliance.

Tiers:

  • Standard: Misconfiguration and vulnerability detection (e.g., public buckets, exposed services).
  • Premium: Threat detection (e.g., crypto mining, container/VM threats, data exfiltration).

Features:

  • Use SCC to enforce org-wide security posture.
  • Integrates with Cloud DLP, Web Security Scanner, Cloud Armor, Forseti, and third-party SIEMs.

Cloud Security Scanner

Web app vulnerability scanner.

Use cases: Detect common OWASP Top 10 issues.

Features:

  • Integrate into CI/CD to scan App Engine, Compute, and GKE endpoints.

Event Threat Detection

Threat detection engine that monitors Cloud Logging for anomalies.

Use cases: Alert on indicators like suspicious SSH access, cryptomining, or privilege escalation.

Features:

  • Real-time detection based on log events.
  • Integrates with SCC and Cloud Monitoring for alerting.

Key & Secret Management

Cloud Key Management Service (KMS)

Manage cryptographic keys for services and applications.

Use cases: Encrypt/decrypt sensitive data, customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK), HSM integration.

Features:

  • Key rings, rotation, IAM integration, audit logging.
  • Use CMEK to control data encryption in services like BigQuery, GCS, GKE, etc.
  • Enforce separation of duties with IAM on keys.

Cloud HSM (Hardware Security Module)

Cloud-based FIPS 140-2 Level 3 certified HSMs.

Use cases: Highly sensitive key material that must stay in hardware.

Features:

  • Integrates with KMS.
  • Required for strict regulatory environments (finance, government).

Secret Manager

Secure storage and access for API keys, passwords, certs, tokens.

Use cases: CI/CD secrets, app config secrets, API credentials.

Features:

  • IAM-secured secrets with audit logging.
  • Use versioning, labels, Pub/Sub-based rotation.
  • Preferred over storing secrets in config files or environment variables.

Policy & Compliance

Organization Policy Service

Enforce constraints across projects or folders (e.g., disable external IPs, enforce CMEK).

Use cases: Governance, compliance, secure baseline enforcement.

Features:

  • Critical for guardrails across large orgs.
  • Use constraint templates for centralized governance.

Cloud Audit Logs

Tracks “who did what, where, and when” on GCP.

Types:

  • Admin Activity (always on, free).
  • System Events (e.g., VM live migration).
  • Data Access (disabled by default; can incur cost).
  • Policy Denied (security policy violation logs).

Features

  • Export to BigQuery, Cloud Storage, or SIEM tools for long-term retention and analysis.

Access Transparency

Logs Google personnel access to your data.

Use cases: Regulatory compliance, enterprise trust.

Features:

  • Only available in premium tiers or for some services (e.g., GCS, BigQuery).

VPC Service Controls

Defines security perimeters around GCP resources to mitigate data exfiltration risks.

Use cases: Secure data across GCS, BigQuery, Pub/Sub, etc.

Features:

  • Prevents accidental or malicious data access outside defined perimeter.
  • Combine with IAM, Cloud Armor, and Private Google Access for full Zero Trust.

Data analytics

Introduction

Data analytics in GCP allows organizations to ingest, store, process, analyze, and visualize data at scale.

These tools are designed to meet the needs of:

  • Data engineers building pipelines.
  • Analysts running interactive queries.
  • Data scientists running ML models.
  • Architects designing real-time or batch-based analytical systems.

Key characteristics of GCP's analytics tools:

  • Serverless and scalable: No infrastructure to manage.
  • Tightly integrated: Works seamlessly with storage (BigQuery), compute (Dataproc/Dataflow), AI (Vertex AI), and security.
  • Multimodal: Batch, streaming, and interactive analysis supported.

Data analytics

BigQuery

Fully managed, serverless data warehouse designed for petabyte-scale SQL analytics.

Use cases:

  • Business intelligence
  • Real-time analytics
  • Data lake analytics
  • Machine learning with BigQuery ML

Key features:

  • ANSI SQL support
  • Storage + compute separation
  • Built-in ML (BigQuery ML), GIS support, and federated queries
  • BI Engine for sub-second dashboarding
  • Use partitioned and clustered tables for performance and cost.
  • Integrates with Cloud Storage, Dataflow, Looker, Vertex AI.
  • Set query quotas, budget alerts, and access control using IAM.

Dataflow

Serverless stream and batch data processing service based on Apache Beam.

Use cases:

  • ETL/ELT pipelines
  • Stream ingestion and transformation
  • Data enrichment and real-time analytics

Key features:

  • Unified model for batch & stream
  • Autoscaling workers
  • Streaming engine for low-latency use cases
  • Good for event-driven or IoT data.
  • Can trigger actions based on processed results.
  • Easily integrates with Pub/Sub, BigQuery, Cloud Storage.

Dataproc

Managed Apache Hadoop/Spark/Presto clusters on GCP.

Use cases:

  • Migrate existing on-prem Hadoop/Spark workloads
  • Machine learning pipelines using PySpark or MLlib
  • ETL and large-scale transformations

Key features:

  • Quick cluster provisioning
  • Preemptible VMs to reduce cost
  • Per-job or ephemeral clusters
  • Ideal when custom libraries or Spark-specific code is used.
  • Use autoscaling clusters and job APIs to optimize cost.
  • Not serverless — you manage clusters and configs.

Pub/Sub

Globally-distributed messaging service for event-driven and streaming architectures.

Use cases:

  • Ingest events from IoT, apps, or systems
  • Decouple microservices
  • Data pipeline triggers

Key features:

  • Scales to millions of messages per second
  • Push and pull delivery models
  • Ordered, at-least-once delivery
  • Combine with Dataflow for near-real-time pipelines.
  • Supports Dead Letter Topics and Message Filtering.
  • Offers exactly-once delivery with Pub/Sub Lite (with tradeoffs).

Dataplex

Intelligent data fabric for managing, organizing, and governing distributed data lakes.

Use cases:

  • Unify data from multiple sources (e.g., BigQuery, GCS)
  • Centralized metadata management and data governance

Key features:

  • Policy-based access
  • Built-in data quality and classification
  • Metadata catalog and lineage tracking
  • Use to govern decentralized storage in data lakes.
  • Integrates with BigQuery, Cloud DLP, Data Catalog.

Data Catalog

Fully managed, metadata discovery and governance service.

Use cases:

  • Organize metadata
  • Search and tag datasets
  • Track lineage

Key features:

  • Google-like search
  • Tag templates and policies
  • Integration with BigQuery, GCS, Pub/Sub
  • Great for self-service analytics environments.
  • Helps with compliance by classifying sensitive fields (e.g., PII).

Looker (BI Platform)

Modern business intelligence and data visualization platform.

Use cases:

  • Dashboards and reporting
  • Embedded analytics
  • Data modeling with LookML

Key features:

  • LookML semantic layer
  • Native BigQuery and multicloud support
  • API-first with embed options
  • Use Looker Blocks to speed development.
  • Ideal for governed BI workflows and embedded analytics.
  • Deeply integrates with BigQuery and Vertex AI for predictive dashboards.

Data Studio / Looker Studio

Free, web-based dashboarding tool.

Use cases:

  • Quick reports and dashboards
  • Marketing, sales, and business data visualization

Key features:

  • Drag-and-drop UI
  • Native GCP and 3rd-party connectors
  • Collaboration and sharing
  • Fast prototyping dashboards over BigQuery or Sheets.
  • Lightweight alternative to Looker for less-governed use cases.

AI & machine learning

Introduction

Google Cloud provides a broad, flexible, and production-grade ecosystem for building, training, and deploying machine learning (ML) models and artificial intelligence (AI) applications. The platform is designed for:

  • Business users and analysts (no ML expertise)
  • Data scientists and ML engineers (hands-on ML dev)
  • DevOps and platform teams (operationalizing and automating ML pipelines)

There are three main approaches supported:

  1. Pre-trained APIs – out-of-the-box models for vision, NLP, translation, speech, and more.
  2. AutoML – no-code training of custom models using your own data.
  3. Custom training – full control of the ML pipeline via code on Vertex AI.

Google Cloud also offers ML Ops, feature stores, managed notebooks, and tools for generative AI development.

AI & ML

Vertex AI

A unified platform for end-to-end ML lifecycle management (data → model → deployment).

Use cases:

  • Custom training and tuning of models
  • Automating ML pipelines (MLOps)
  • Deploying models with monitoring and rollback

Key features:

  • Supports AutoML, custom training, and LLMs
  • Built-in Feature Store, Model Registry, and Model Monitoring
  • Vertex AI Workbench for notebooks and collaboration
  • Use pipelines for automated CI/CD for ML.
  • Monitor model drift, training logs, and prediction latency.
  • Tight integration with BigQuery, GCS, Cloud Logging, Cloud Build.

AutoML (in Vertex AI)

No-code model training solution that lets you build custom models via a simple UI.

Use cases:

  • Image, text, and tabular classification or regression
  • Custom NLP tasks with minimal ML experience

Key features:

  • Point-and-click interface
  • Uses neural architecture search and transfer learning
  • Ensemble predictions from top models
  • Ideal for low-code environments and MVPs.
  • Training costs can grow with dataset size — manage budgets.
  • Easily deploy models to Vertex AI endpoints.

Vertex AI Model Garden

A hub of pre-trained and fine-tunable models, including Google’s foundation models (e.g., PaLM) and open-source models.

Use cases:

  • Accelerate LLM integration (e.g., chatbots, summarization)
  • Evaluate and fine-tune pre-built models

Key features:

  • Includes text, code, image, and multimodal models
  • Easy deployment into your apps or pipelines
  • Can be invoked using APIs or integrated into workflows.
  • Consider budget implications of foundation models (token-based billing).
  • Ensure prompt engineering and output validation for GenAI tasks.

Pre-trained AI APIs

Fully managed REST APIs for vision, video, text, translation, speech, and more.

Use cases:

  • OCR, face/object detection, transcription, translation
  • Sentiment analysis, content moderation

Available APIs:

  • Vision AI, Speech-to-Text, Text-to-Speech
  • Natural Language API
  • Translation API, Video Intelligence API

Features:

  • No training needed — plug-and-play via REST or SDK.
  • Ensure rate-limiting, latency monitoring, and auth (API keys, OAuth).
  • Use quota management and error handling in production.

Vertex AI Workbench

A managed Jupyter-based notebook environment for data science workflows.

Use cases:

  • Exploratory data analysis, model development, ML experimentation

Key features:

  • Deep integration with BigQuery, GCS, Git, and AI APIs
  • Supports Python, TensorFlow, scikit-learn, PyTorch, etc.
  • Use Workbenches with idle shutdown to manage cost.
  • Ideal for team collaboration and hybrid workloads.
  • Supports GPU and TPU acceleration.

AI Platform Prediction (legacy)

The older model hosting and prediction service (now part of Vertex AI).

Use cases:

  • Hosting TensorFlow/Scikit-learn models

Key features:

  • Batch or online predictions
  • Migrate to Vertex AI for modern features and better integration.

Tensor Processing Units (TPUs)

Google-designed accelerators optimized for deep learning tasks.

Use cases:

  • High-performance training and inference of deep neural networks

Key features:

  • Faster than GPUs for many TensorFlow models
  • Available in Vertex AI training jobs
  • Choose TPU versions carefully (v2, v3, v4) depending on model requirements.
  • Requires code tuning — not a plug-in GPU replacement.
  • Use with Vertex AI custom training or GKE.

Generative AI Studio (Vertex AI Studio)

A low-code UI and SDK environment for building GenAI-powered applications.

Use cases:

  • Prompt tuning, synthetic data generation, summarization, chatbots

Key features:

  • Playground for text, image, and multimodal model experiments
  • Fine-tuning tools, embeddings, and tuning datasets
  • Great for early experimentation and proof-of-concept work.
  • Move projects to production using Vertex AI endpoints and APIs.

Dialogflow CX

A visual builder for conversational AI, designed to develop chatbots and voicebots.

Use cases:

  • Customer service, call center bots, virtual agents

Key features:

  • Flow-based dialog design
  • Integrates with telephony and web-based channels
  • Connect bots to GCP services (Pub/Sub, GCS, BigQuery).
  • Secure with IAM and monitor with Cloud Logging.
  • Use Dialogflow webhook for backend integrations.

Developer & DevOps tools

Introduction

Google Cloud offers a rich ecosystem of tools to support the entire DevOps lifecycle:

  • Development (IDE integrations, APIs, SDKs)
  • Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery (CI/CD)
  • Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
  • Artifact management
  • Security automation (DevSecOps)

These tools are essential for building scalable, secure, and high-performing cloud-native applications, and automating deployment pipelines and infrastructure provisioning.

As a Cloud DevOps Engineer or Architect, these tools enable:

  • Faster development and release cycles
  • Greater reliability and reproducibility
  • Enforced policy and security compliance
  • Scalable infrastructure orchestration

Tools

Cloud Build

Google Cloud’s fully managed CI/CD platform.

Use cases:

  • Automate builds, tests, and deployments.
  • Containerize apps and push to Artifact Registry.

Key features:

  • Supports Docker, Maven, Gradle, Bazel, npm, etc.
  • Easily integrates with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket.
  • Native YAML-based pipeline definitions.
  • Use Cloud Build triggers to auto-run pipelines on Git events.
  • Secure builds using private pools and Worker Pools.
  • Integrate Binary Authorization for trusted container promotion.

Artifact Registry

A central repository for storing and managing build artifacts.

Use cases:

  • Container images (Docker), Helm charts, Java, Python, npm packages.

Key features:

  • Replaces Container Registry (gcr.io)
  • Regional and multi-regional repositories
  • IAM-based fine-grained access control
  • Integrate with Cloud Build, GKE, and CI tools.
  • Enforce vulnerability scanning and promotion workflows.

Cloud Deploy

A managed continuous delivery service for deploying applications to GKE, Cloud Run, and Anthos.

Use cases:

  • Automate multi-stage delivery pipelines.
  • Promote releases across environments (dev → staging → prod).

Key features:

  • Supports approvals, rollbacks, and release strategies.
  • GitOps-style delivery
  • Use for multi-env progressive delivery with visibility and control.
  • Combine with Cloud Build for full CI/CD.
  • Integrate with Skaffold for easy Kubernetes development.

Skaffold

A command-line tool that simplifies Kubernetes development workflows.

Use cases:

  • Local development with GKE/Minikube.
  • Automating build-push-deploy loop.

Key features:

  • Watch mode, automatic rebuild & redeploy on file changes.
  • Compatible with Cloud Build, Docker, Kubernetes manifests.
  • Use in combination with Cloud Build and Cloud Deploy.
  • Useful in GitOps and iterative development environments.

Cloud Source Repositories

A private Git repository service hosted on Google Cloud.

Use cases:

  • Store and manage source code.
  • Integrate directly with Cloud Build triggers.

Key features:

  • Native IAM permissions
  • Code search and mirroring from GitHub/Bitbucket
  • Good for organizations wanting fully GCP-managed source hosting.
  • Can mirror GitHub to enable GCP-native CI/CD.

Cloud Code

IDE plugins for Visual Studio Code and IntelliJ IDEA.

Use cases:

  • Develop, debug, and deploy cloud-native applications directly from IDE.

Key features:

  • Supports Kubernetes, Cloud Run, GKE, and App Engine.
  • Integrated diagnostics, logging, YAML editing.
  • Great for enabling local development parity with remote GCP services.
  • Boosts developer productivity while maintaining infra alignment.

Cloud Scheduler

A managed cron job service for scheduling tasks.

Use cases:

  • Trigger jobs via HTTP, Pub/Sub, or Cloud Functions.
  • Use in pipelines for timed operations (nightly builds, cleanup).

Key features:

  • Retry logic, monitoring, timezone support
  • Replace traditional cron/Quartz jobs.
  • Secure with IAM + service accounts.
  • Monitor execution via Cloud Logging.

Cloud Tasks

Asynchronous task queue service.

Use cases:

  • Offload long-running HTTP workloads (e.g., retries, queuing)

Key features:

  • Rate limiting, retry policies, dead-letter queues
  • Useful for decoupling microservices and preventing overload.
  • Monitor and control task lifecycle for background processing pipelines.

Firebase App Distribution (for CI/CD with Firebase)

A way to distribute pre-release mobile builds to testers.

Use cases:

  • Test mobile apps before publishing.

Key features:

  • Send updates via email or link.
  • Integrates with CI/CD (Cloud Build, GitHub Actions).
  • Important for mobile DevOps workflows.
  • Combine with Crashlytics + Cloud Functions for feedback loop.

Monitoring, logging & operations

Introduction

Cloud operations in Google Cloud are centered around the Google Cloud Operations Suite (formerly Stackdriver), a fully integrated observability platform for:

  • Monitoring: system health and performance
  • Logging: event and audit data tracking
  • Tracing: latency and request flow visualization
  • Profiling: performance bottleneck detection
  • Alerting: proactive issue notification
  • Debugging: real-time inspection of production apps

As a Cloud DevOps Engineer or Architect, your responsibilities include ensuring availability, reliability, and performance of applications. These tools help achieve that through observability, automated diagnostics, and incident response capabilities.

Products

Cloud Monitoring

A fully managed metrics collection and dashboarding service.

Use cases:

  • Visualize system and application performance.
  • Create SLOs, SLIs, and dashboards.
  • Set alerts on thresholds or anomalies.

Key features:

  • Native integration with GCP services (Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud Run).
  • Predefined and custom metrics.
  • Supports uptime checks and alerting policies.
  • Use SLO-based alerting for business-critical services.
  • Group and scope metrics across multi-project workspaces.
  • Monitor custom apps or third-party tools with the Ops Agent or OpenTelemetry.

Cloud Logging

Centralized log aggregation, querying, and analysis system.

Use cases:

  • Collect logs from all GCP services and VMs.
  • Search, filter, and create alerts from logs.
  • Export logs to BigQuery, Pub/Sub, or Cloud Storage.

Key features:

  • Near real-time ingestion.
  • Logs Explorer for queries and visualizations.
  • Retention policies and exclusion filters.
  • Use log-based metrics for alerting or dashboarding.
  • Export logs for long-term storage or SIEM integration.
  • Secure with IAM roles (Logs Viewer, Private Logs Viewer).

Cloud Trace

A distributed tracing system for latency analysis.

Use cases:

  • Track end-to-end request flows.
  • Diagnose latency bottlenecks in microservices.

Key features:

  • Visual per-request traces.
  • Automatic instrumentation for App Engine, GKE, Cloud Run.
  • Use in microservice and hybrid app environments.
  • Integrate with OpenTelemetry SDKs for custom tracing.

Cloud Profiler

A low-overhead sampling profiler for production apps.

Use cases:

  • Identify CPU, memory, and thread performance issues.

Key features:

  • Supports Java, Go, Node.js, and Python.
  • Always-on profiling with minimal overhead.
  • Use for cost optimization and improving app performance.
  • Combine with Cloud Trace to correlate slow traces with CPU bottlenecks.

Error Reporting

Real-time error detection and alerting system.

Use cases:

  • Track exceptions and stack traces.
  • Alert when new or regressed errors occur.

Key features:

  • Aggregates similar errors.
  • Links to relevant source lines.
  • Use for fast response to critical failures.
  • Integrate with Slack, PagerDuty, or email for incident alerting.

Cloud Debugger

Live debugging tool for production apps.

Use cases:

  • Inspect application state without stopping the app.

Key features:

  • Read-only breakpoints.
  • Snapshot variables and stack traces.
  • Use to safely debug live issues with zero performance impact.
  • Supports App Engine, Cloud Run, and Compute Engine with agent.

Ops Agent

Unified agent for collecting logs and metrics from VMs.

Use cases:

  • Replace legacy logging/monitoring agents.
  • Collect metrics from third-party software (Apache, NGINX, MySQL).

Key features:

  • One agent, multiple sources (logs + metrics).
  • Simple deployment via Cloud Console, scripts, or Terraform.
  • Use in custom apps or multi-cloud workloads.
  • Ensure visibility of all workloads with low overhead telemetry.

Cloud Audit Logs

Immutable logging system for all user and admin activities.

Use cases:

  • Track who did what, where, and when.

Key features:

  • Four types: Admin Activity, Data Access, System Events, Policy Denied.
  • Retention: Admin & System = 400 days; Data Access = 30 days.
  • Essential for compliance and incident response.
  • Export logs to BigQuery for analysis or to SIEMs for security correlation.
  • Use Private Logs Viewer role to secure sensitive logs.

Monitoring Dashboards, Alerting, and Uptime Checks

Visualization and notification services for system status.

Use cases:

  • Real-time dashboards, alert routing, and SLA validation.

Key features:

  • Drag-and-drop dashboard builder.
  • Alert policies based on metrics or logs.
  • Uptime checks with HTTP/S or TCP.
  • Use multi-project dashboards in cross-org scenarios.
  • Integrate alerting with Slack, PagerDuty, Opsgenie, SMS, or email.
  • Design dashboards with SLO/SLI visualizations for reliability goals.

Best practices

  • Use log-based metrics for alerting on errors or performance conditions.
  • Define SLOs/SLIs and monitor them via dashboards for production reliability.
  • Aggregate and correlate metrics, logs, and traces to troubleshoot fast.

  • Continuously export logs to BigQuery for historical analysis or compliance.

Integration & API

Introduction

Integration and API management services in GCP allow teams to:

  • Seamlessly connect disparate systems and applications (cloud, on-prem, SaaS).
  • Expose, manage, and secure APIs as products to internal or external developers.
  • Build event-driven architectures, hybrid cloud applications, and workflow automations.

These services are critical for implementing service-oriented architecture (SOA), microservices, and event-driven pipelines — common patterns in modern cloud-native solutions.

Products

Apigee API Management

A full-featured API management platform for designing, securing, publishing, monitoring, and analyzing APIs.

Use cases:

  • Monetize APIs for partners or customers.
  • Secure and throttle backend services.
  • Version and analyze API usage trends.

Key features:

  • API gateways, security policies (OAuth2, JWT, quota, caching).
  • Developer portal, analytics, and monetization.
  • Supports hybrid (on-prem + cloud) and multi-cloud deployments.
  • Use Apigee for enterprise-grade API governance.
  • Integrate with IAM, Cloud Armor, and Cloud CDN for layered security.
  • Valuable in external API exposure and third-party integration scenarios.

API Gateway

A lightweight, fully managed gateway to create, secure, and monitor APIs.

Use cases:

  • Manage internal microservice APIs.
  • Integrate with Cloud Functions and Cloud Run.

Key features:

  • Supports OpenAPI spec.
  • IAM-based authentication.
  • Scales automatically and integrates with Cloud Logging and Monitoring.
  • Ideal for internal service-to-service APIs.
  • Use for lower-cost, lower-complexity scenarios than Apigee.
  • Combine with Firebase Authentication or IAM for securing APIs.

Cloud Tasks

A fully managed asynchronous task queue.

Use cases:

  • Offload background jobs from front-end apps.
  • Rate-limit workloads hitting external APIs.

Key features:

  • Scheduled and retryable task execution.
  • HTTP-based task handlers (e.g., Cloud Run, App Engine).
  • Integrates with IAM and supports task deduplication.
  • Useful in decoupled microservices or serverless backends.
  • Add rate limits, retries, and exponential backoff for resilient pipelines.

Cloud Pub/Sub

A serverless messaging middleware for real-time, event-driven systems.

Use cases:

  • Event ingestion and broadcasting between services.
  • Data streaming pipelines.

Key features:

  • Publish-subscribe messaging model.
  • Push and pull delivery, dead letter queues, and replay.
  • Global scale, up to millions of messages per second.
  • Core for event-driven and microservice communication.
  • Combine with Dataflow or BigQuery for real-time analytics pipelines.
  • Use IAM to restrict publish/subscribe access.

Eventarc

A fully managed event routing service that lets you build loosely coupled event-driven apps.

Use cases:

  • Trigger Cloud Run services based on events from GCP or custom apps.
  • Enable cloud-native CI/CD triggers.

Key features:

  • Supports Cloud Audit Logs, Pub/Sub, custom sources.
  • Built on CloudEvents standard.
  • Ideal for decoupled serverless workflows.
  • Useful for security event responses and resource monitoring triggers.
  • Compatible with hybrid/cloud event sources.

Workflows

A serverless orchestration engine to coordinate Google Cloud services and APIs.

Use cases:

  • Define complex business logic (approval chains, async branches).
  • Integrate across services (Cloud Functions, Run, Pub/Sub).

Key features:

  • YAML-based workflow definitions.
  • Error handling, retries, and branching logic.
  • Use to orchestrate microservices or multi-step cloud automation.
  • Great for event-triggered business logic across services.
  • Secure workflows with IAM and integrate with Service Accounts.

Connectors (via Application Integration or Workflows)

Pre-built connectors to SaaS systems and databases.

Use cases:

  • Integrate with Salesforce, SAP, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and other systems.

Key features:

  • Ready-to-use integrations with minimal coding.
  • Can be used inside Workflows or Apigee Integrations.
  • Accelerates data integration and B2B flows.
  • Simplifies legacy modernization and hybrid workflows.

DevOps/Architect Value

Best practices

  • Use Pub/Sub for scalable, event-driven patterns in microservices.
  • Secure APIs exposed through API Gateway or Apigee with IAM, OAuth, or Cloud Armor.
  • Use Cloud Tasks to buffer HTTP requests and control rate limits in backends.
  • Orchestrate multi-step operations and error handling with Workflows.
  • Leverage Eventarc to build reactive infrastructure, such as CI/CD triggers or incident responders.
  • Integrate external systems using connectors and monitor their data flow using Cloud Monitoring.


Hybrid & multi-cloud

Introduction

Hybrid and multi-cloud solutions in GCP are designed to:

  • Bridge on-premises infrastructure with cloud-native services.
  • Enable multi-cloud portability and consistency.
  • Support regulatory, compliance, or latency requirements that require workloads to remain partially on-prem or on alternative clouds.

These services empower DevOps teams and architects to manage workloads consistently across environments, extend Kubernetes clusters, enforce security, and unify operations — whether workloads run in Google Cloud, on-prem, or other public clouds like AWS or Azure.

Products

Anthos

A modern application management platform for hybrid and multi-cloud Kubernetes.

Use cases:

  • Consistent K8s management across on-prem, GCP, and other clouds.
  • Centralized policy enforcement and service mesh observability.

Key features:

  • Anthos Config Management (ACM): declarative config and policy-as-code.
  • Anthos Service Mesh (ASM): built on Istio, provides zero-trust networking.
  • Works with GKE, GKE On-Prem, AWS, and Azure.
  • Anthos enables GitOps, SRE, and compliance-at-scale practices.
  • Use Anthos Config Sync to manage fleet-wide policies from a central repo.
  • Offers consistent developer experience regardless of runtime location.

GKE Enterprise (formerly Anthos GKE)

The enterprise-grade Kubernetes offering that extends GKE to on-premises and other clouds.

Use cases:

  • Run GKE consistently across hybrid and multi-cloud environments.
  • Manage clusters centrally using GKE Hub and Fleet.

Key features:

  • GKE Autopilot and Standard modes.
  • Fleet management for cluster grouping, config sync, policy enforcement.
  • Mesh integration, workload identity, and observability.
  • Ideal for central governance, multi-cluster workloads, and fleet policies.
  • Use Workload Identity Federation for secure service-to-service auth.
  • Monitor hybrid workloads via Cloud Monitoring and Logging.

BigQuery Omni

A multi-cloud analytics solution that lets you query data stored in AWS and Azure using standard BigQuery SQL, without moving the data.

Use cases:

  • Federated queries across clouds for cost savings and data residency.
  • Unified analytics dashboard for multi-cloud data pipelines.

Key features:

  • Data remains in AWS/Azure, compute is proximate to data.
  • Supports federated joins and analytics workflows.
  • Minimizes data egress costs and compliance challenges.
  • Use for multi-cloud data lakehouse architectures.
  • Combine with Looker or Dataform for unified BI.

Cloud Interconnect

A dedicated private connectivity solution to Google Cloud from your on-premises environment.

Use cases:

  • High-bandwidth, low-latency connectivity for hybrid workloads.

Key features:

  • Dedicated Interconnect (10 Gbps or 100 Gbps).
  • Partner Interconnect through carriers.
  • Can be combined with VPC Network Peering.
  • Use for hybrid clusters, low-latency DB access, or backup traffic.
  • Consider HA VLANs for reliability.
  • Integrate with Private Google Access for secure service endpoints.

Cloud VPN

A secure IPsec VPN tunnel between your network and GCP.

Use cases:

  • Secure hybrid connectivity without the cost of dedicated lines.

Key features:

  • Static or dynamic routing (BGP).
  • HA VPN for high-availability architecture.
  • Ideal for fast hybrid onboarding or low-volume hybrid traffic.
  • Combine with Cloud Router for dynamic routing.

Traffic Director

GCP’s fully managed service mesh traffic control plane for hybrid and multi-cloud deployments.

Use cases:

  • Service discovery, traffic routing, and resiliency across environments.

Key features:

  • Manages Envoy-based sidecar proxies.
  • Global load balancing, canary deployment support.
  • Core to service mesh implementation in hybrid/multi-cloud.
  • Combine with Anthos Service Mesh or Istio.
  • Use for zero-trust service-to-service auth with mTLS.

Migrate to Virtual Machines (Migrate to VMs)

A tool to lift and shift on-prem VMs to Google Compute Engine.

Use cases:

  • Move workloads to the cloud without needing to re-architect.

Key features:

  • Supports VMware, AWS, Azure, Hyper-V.
  • Batch or continuous replication, testing before cutover.
  • Simplifies initial cloud migration phase.
  • Use for legacy workloads not yet containerized.

Migrate to Containers

A tool that automatically transforms VMs into containers for deployment on GKE or Anthos.

Use cases:

  • Refactor legacy workloads for cloud-native architecture.

Key features:

  • Extracts app + dependencies, packages into OCI-compliant containers.
  • Compatible with GKE, Artifact Registry.
  • Great for modernization journeys.
  • Combine with Cloud Build and Artifact Registry for CI/CD workflows.

Best practices

  • Use Anthos Config Management and Service Mesh to enforce consistency and observability across environments.
  • Consider BigQuery Omni when data sovereignty or multi-cloud analytics are priorities.
  • Prefer Cloud Interconnect for high-throughput, low-latency hybrid traffic; use Cloud VPN for lower scale needs.
  • Use Workload Identity Federation across hybrid services to reduce key rotation burden.
  • Migrate apps with Migrate to VMs initially, then Migrate to Containers as part of long-term modernization strategy.


Management & governance

Introduction

Management and Governance tools in Google Cloud help organizations:

  • Control billing, resource access, and policy enforcement.
  • Implement cost visibility, compliance, organization structure, and resource hierarchy.
  • Ensure consistent and secure configurations across projects.
  • Simplify auditing, quota management, and multi-project operations.

This category is essential for DevOps and Cloud Architects to scale cloud adoption securely, enforce operational consistency, and maintain control in large or complex environments.

Products

Cloud Resource Manager

Manages the GCP resource hierarchy — Organizations, Folders, and Projects.

Use Cases:

  • Structuring resources by teams, departments, or environments.
  • Applying policies or IAM permissions at different levels.

Key Features:

  • Enables centralized control using Org Policies and IAM.
  • Folders allow grouping of projects with inherited policies.
  • Best practice is to group projects by environment (prod, staging, dev).
  • Apply IAM and Org Policy inheritance to reduce redundancy.

Cloud Billing

Centralized billing management platform for GCP.

Use Cases:

  • Manage multiple accounts and link projects to billing.
  • Set budgets and alerts for cost control.

Key Features:

  • Budgeting and alerting tools.
  • Export billing data to BigQuery for analysis.
  • Use budgets + Pub/Sub alerts to automate cost remediation.
  • Integrate with Looker Studio or BigQuery for cost dashboards.

Cloud Identity & Access Management (IAM)

Fine-grained authorization framework for resources.

Use Cases:

  • Define who can access what, and what actions they can perform.

Key Features:

  • Supports roles (basic, predefined, custom).
  • Resource-level granularity.
  • Follow the Principle of Least Privilege.
  • Prefer predefined roles over custom ones when possible.

Policy Intelligence

Set of tools to analyze and optimize IAM policies.

Use Cases:

  • Detect excessive permissions, unused access.

Key Features:

  • Policy Analyzer, Policy Troubleshooter, Recommender.
  • Run IAM Recommender regularly to eliminate over-provisioning.
  • Use Policy Troubleshooter for fast debugging of access issues.

Resource Manager Tags

Key-value metadata tags applied to resources.

Use Cases:

  • Label resources for cost attribution, ownership, or automation.

Key Features:

  • Hierarchical tag policies enforced by Org Policy.
  • Use tags to automate guardrails, e.g., prevent public IP assignment in prod.
  • Enforce with Org Policy + Tag bindings.

Cloud Asset Inventory

Inventory and metadata database of GCP resources.

Use Cases:

  • Search and export asset metadata.
  • Audit configurations and IAM policies.

Key Features:

  • Real-time and historical snapshots.
  • Integrates with SCC and BigQuery.
  • Use for compliance audits, IAM visibility, and resource drift detection.

Cloud Config (formerly Config Controller)

Managed Kubernetes-based configuration controller using Config Connector + Anthos Config Management.

Use Cases:

  • Apply Infrastructure-as-Code using Kubernetes CRDs.

Key Features:

  • GitOps with support for GCP resources.
  • Works with Policy Controller and OPA for validation.
  • Enforce infrastructure policies as code.
  • Best for teams already using KRM (Kubernetes Resource Model).

Cloud Deployment Manager

GCP’s native Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) tool.

Use Cases:

  • Automate the creation of resources via YAML configuration files.

Key Features:

  • Declarative templates in YAML/Jinja/Python.
  • Best for small-scale deployments or orgs already invested in it.
  • Consider using Terraform for broader IaC needs.

Cloud Quotas

Resource limits imposed by GCP to prevent abuse and overconsumption.

Use Cases:

  • Prevent runaway resource usage or billing surprises.

Key Features:

  • Adjustable per project or per region.
  • Alerts on approaching limits.
  • Set budget alerts and quota dashboards.
  • Use quotas to simulate “resource sandboxing” for dev teams.

Assured Workloads

GCP solution to enforce compliance controls like FedRAMP, CJIS, HIPAA, etc.

Use Cases:

  • Host sensitive workloads with compliance requirements.

Key Features:

  • Region/data residency control.
  • Vetted personnel and compliance zones.
  • Helps with compliance-driven projects.
  • Combine with VPC-SC, DLP, and CMEK for full regulatory stack.

Organizational Policy Service (Org Policy)

Define and enforce organization-wide constraints on GCP usage.

Use Cases:

  • Prevent creation of resources outside approved regions.
  • Block usage of unapproved services or configurations.

Key Features:

  • Applied at org, folder, or project level.
  • Supports constraint inheritance.
  • Use to enforce compliance, security, and cost policies at scale.
  • Combine with Policy Intelligence and Tags for powerful enforcement.

Networking

What it is?

Google Network is a high-performance, private global infrastructure that connects Google Cloud data centers, regional locations, and users worldwide. It is designed for speed, scalability, security, and reliability, leveraging software-defined networking (SDN) and distributed systems to efficiently manage and deliver cloud services.


Networking is a fundamental aspect of cloud computing, enabling computers to communicate with each other efficiently. Networks can be classified as:

  • Local Area Networks (LANs): Networks connecting computers within a single location, such as an office.
  • Wide Area Networks (WANs): Networks that connect multiple LANs, often across different locations.
  • Internet Connectivity: Most modern networks are connected to the internet, allowing devices like personal computers, smartphones, and servers to interact and provide IT services.


Google has built a high-speed, private cloud infrastructure since 2004, setting industry standards for performance and reliability. The key aspects of Google's network include:

  • Global Connectivity: Google’s private network connects regional locations to over 100 global network points of presence (PoPs), ensuring low-latency and high-speed connectivity.
  • Software-Defined Networking (SDN): Google Cloud uses state-of-the-art SDN and distributed systems to efficiently manage data flow and cloud service delivery.
  • Optimized Content Delivery: To minimize latency, Google ensures content delivery with the highest throughput, optimizing user experience.


Advantages

  1. Global Private Infrastructure

    • Google operates one of the world’s largest private cloud networks.
    • Over 100 global network points of presence (PoPs) ensure low-latency access for users.
    • Connects regional locations, data centers, and cloud resources through dedicated fiber-optic connections.

  2. Software-Defined Networking (SDN)

    • Uses state-of-the-art SDN for efficient traffic management and network automation.
    • Ensures high throughput and minimal latency in cloud-based services.

  3. Content Delivery Optimization

    • Google Cloud CDN caches frequently accessed content closer to users, improving speed.
    • Requests for uncached content are routed through Cloud Load Balancing, which selects the best available server.

  4. Cloud Load Balancing

    • Distributes traffic intelligently across multiple Compute Engine instances.
    • Optimizes performance based on server availability, geographic proximity, and resource utilization.

  5. Isolated Network Resources

    • Google Cloud defines networks as global resources, but instances are deployed in regional subnetworks.
    • Firewall, routing, and VPN policies are controlled at the global network level.
    • Security Isolation: Frontend servers are restricted from directly accessing backend data centers.

  6. Fast and Secure Data Transmission

    • Google’s network ensures that every millisecond of latency counts.
    • Uses end-to-end encryption to protect data in transit.

How it works

Components

Google Cloud’s network infrastructure enables seamless connectivity between on-premises data centers and cloud-hosted applications. Below are the main components:

  1. Domain Name System (DNS) Resolution

    • When a user makes a request, it goes through Cloud DNS, which resolves the requested domain name to an IP address.

  2. Content Delivery Network (CDN)

    • Google Cloud provides CDNs to cache content closer to users, reducing latency and improving performance.
    • If a requested page is cached at a CDN location, it is served directly without contacting backend servers.
    • If the page is not cached, the request is forwarded to Cloud Load Balancing.

  3. Cloud Load Balancing

    • Cloud Load Balancing dynamically selects an appropriate frontend server based on factors such as geographical location and server availability.
    • The load balancer ensures that traffic is distributed efficiently across Compute Engine instances in different regions.

  4. Compute Engine and Backend Communication

    • Frontend Compute Engine servers handle user requests.
    • These servers may need to fetch data from backend Compute Engine servers, which are updated regularly from other sources.
    • Subnetworks are configured with security rules to control access between frontend servers, backend servers, and external data centers.

  5. Network Configuration and Policies

    • In Google Cloud, a "network" is a globally available resource that holds network configurations, including:

      • Firewall rules
      • Routing policies
      • VPN access control
    • Instances are deployed in regional subnetworks, but policies are managed at the global network level.

  6. Security and Isolation

    • Google Cloud isolates network resources to enhance security and optimize performance.
    • Example: The frontend subnet cannot directly communicate with the data center or colocation facility, ensuring controlled access to sensitive infrastructure.

Products

VPC

What it is?

A Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) in Google Cloud is a foundational networking component enabling Google Cloud administrators to create and manage isolated network environments for their resources.


A Google Cloud Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) is a virtualized network that provides scalable and secure networking for Google Cloud resources. It allows administrators to define network configurations, including IP address ranges, subnets, and routing rules, offering the flexibility to build custom network architectures.

Key features

Global rreach

  • VPCs are global resources, meaning they span all regions. Subnets within a VPC, however, are regional.
  • This global nature allows seamless communication between resources across regions within the same VPC.

Customizable sssubnets

  • Subnets are defined by IP ranges using CIDR (Classless Inter-Domain Routing).
  • Administrators can create subnets in specific regions, allowing precise control over resource placement.

Private Google Access

  • Enables access to Google services without needing a public IP.

Dynamic and Static Routing

  • Supports custom route configurations using static routes.
  • Dynamic routing allows automatic route management using Cloud Router and BGP (Border Gateway Protocol).

Peering and Connectivity Options

  • VPC Peering: Connects two VPCs for internal communication.
  • Shared VPC: Allows multiple projects to use a centrally managed VPC.
  • Interconnect and VPN: For hybrid connectivity between on-premises and Google Cloud.

Firewall Rules

  • Customizable firewall rules control inbound and outbound traffic at the instance level.
  • Stateful rules ensure consistency in session management.

Flow Logs

  • VPC Flow Logs provide detailed traffic analysis for network monitoring and troubleshooting.

Modes

Google Cloud offers two types of VPC networks, based on how subnets are created:

Auto Mode VPC

  • Automatically creates one subnet per Google Cloud region.
  • New subnets are automatically added when new regions become available.
  • Uses predefined IP ranges for each region.
  • Allows manually adding subnets with custom IP ranges.
  • The broadest possible prefix for an expanded IP range is /16.

  • Better suited for:

    • Proof of concepts (PoC)
    • Testing environments
    • Simple, isolated use cases

  • Limitations:

    • Less flexibility in subnet and IP range control.
    • Cannot revert back to Auto Mode if switched to Custom Mode.

Custom Mode VPC

  • Subnets are not created automatically—users must manually define them.
  • Provides full control over subnet creation, regions, and IP ranges.
  • IP ranges cannot overlap between subnets in the same network.
  • More flexible and scalable for production use cases.

  • Better suited for:

    • Production environments
    • Complex, large-scale deployments

Advanced networking configurations

Advanced features

Shared VPC

    • Share a VPC across multiple projects in the same organization.
    • Centralize network administration while allowing project-level resource management.

VPC Peering

    • Low-latency internal communication between two VPCs.
    • Ideal for connecting VPCs in different projects or organizations.

Hybrid Connectivity

    • Cloud Interconnect: High-bandwidth, low-latency dedicated connections.
    • Cloud VPN: Encrypted connectivity over public networks.

Private Services Access

    • Connects VPC networks with managed services using private IPs.
    • Commonly used for accessing services like Cloud SQL or Memorystore.
